On Fri, Aug 19, 2028 at 09:12 AM Olivia Torres <olivia.torres@heliomed.com> wrote:
> Thanks for the demo yesterday — the team is excited to move the pilot forward. Attached is a marked-up contract with a few items we need to address before procurement can issue an SOW: 1) a 40% pilot discount for year one, 2) changes to the indemnity to make HelioMed responsible for third-party claims arising from our integration work, and 3) broader warranty language around uptime and data retention.

Quick take: the opportunity is strategically valuable (HelioMed is a potential enterprise reference in med-dev space) but the ask exceeds our standard delegation: >25% discount and substantive indemnity changes. Financials: list price year-1 = $180,000; 40% would bring ARR-first-year to ~$108k (delta vs standard ~$72k).

Proposed commercial counter (two options):
A) Accept 30% pilot discount, require 12-month minimum term, put liability cap at $500k (or 2x pilot fees), and require customer-signed security addendum. Legal to keep standard indemnity (we indemnify for IP infringement; customer responsible for customer data misuse).
B) Approve up to 35% discount only if exec sign-off is given to accept revised indemnity language (mutual indemnity for third-party claims limited to direct IP claims) and raise liability cap to $750k.

I attached updated pricing matrix showing P&L impact. I think option B is defensible if leadership will accept the limited legal concessions — HelioMed is high-value and on a fast timeline. Requesting exec clearance for option B.

Attachments: pricing_matrix_helio_v2.xlsx

- Ben
Senior Director, Strategic Accounts
ben_carter@redwood.com
From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: ben_carter@redwood.com, stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com
Date: 2028-08-19T18:05:00Z
Subject: Re: Contract redlines + discount request for pilot

Thanks for the context. I reviewed HelioMed's redlines and summarized the legal exposure and recommended language below. Per policy, any change that increases our liability exposure above $500k or that alters core indemnities requires executive sign-off.

Key redline points and recommended position:
1) Indemnity shifts: HelioMed has attempted to make us indemnify their third-party claims linked to integration work. We should not accept blanket transfers of responsibility. Recommend mutual indemnity for IP infringement only; reject language that places indemnity for integration/configuration errors on Redwood. If customer insists, require scope-limited carveout tied to vendor-provided integration services and additional fee.

2) Liability cap: We typically cap aggregate liability at the greater of fees paid or $250k. Given strategic value, legal can accept a cap of up to $750k for this pilot if (a) we get a 12-month minimum commitment or (b) HelioMed purchases an extended warranty add-on. Also require consequential damages waiver and reinsure any punitive claims.

3) Warranty: Remove open-ended uptime warranty; propose SLA with remedies limited to service credits up to a small percentage of monthly fees. Require tech validation and limit warranty period to 30 days post-deployment for performance claims.

4) Security & compliance: Add a required security addendum (SOC 2 Type II attestation or equivalent). No production go-live until we have SOC 2 evidence or a documented compensating control.

Action items for escalation:
- Sales to get exec approval for any discount >25% or liability cap >$500k (Ben, please escalate).
- Legal to prepare a clean counter with redline reflecting the above (I will attach a draft shortly).

Related: JIRA SUP-8593 created to track document evidence requests.

—Marissa Cole
General Counsel, Redwood Inference

Subject: Exec approval request — HelioMed pilot (discount + indemnity)

Aditya — quick executive summary and ask.

Opportunity: HelioMed pilot; potential enterprise reference in med-dev vertical. Forecasted first-year spend ~ $180k. 

Customer asks: 40% pilot discount; they redlined indemnity to reduce their responsibility for third-party claims; requests broader warranty language. Procurement is requesting a PO by next Friday.

Options (recommended):
- Option A (conservative): Approve 25% discount (within delegated authority), maintain standard indemnity, liability cap at $500k. 
- Option B (recommended for fast close): Approve up to 30% discount, accept a limited revision to indemnity (mutual IP indemnity; reject operational/implementation indemnity), raise liability cap to $750k, require 12-month term and executed security addendum. Legal sign-off required before countersign.

Why B: accelerates close, gives us a high-profile reference, incremental revenue offset by the security addendum and term commitment; legal has drafted mitigations. Downside: modestly higher liability exposure — requires exec OK.

Attachments: pricing impact, legal summary, customer redline. Please reply with OK to proceed on Option B or provide alternative direction.

—Stephanie
Enterprise Sales Manager, Redwood Inference
stephanie_nguyen@redwood.com

Date: 2028-08-19T20:03:00Z
Subject: Re: Exec approval request — HelioMed pilot (discount + indemnity)

Thanks for the concise summary. Approved with conditions:
- Approve Option B but cap pilot discount at 30% (not 35%).
- Liability cap may be increased to $750k for the pilot only and only if HelioMed signs the security addendum and commits to a 12-month minimum term or a signed PO covering the pilot fees.
- Legal to finalize the counter (mutual IP indemnity; no transfer of integration risk to Redwood).
- Sales ops to confirm PO/commitment before countersigning.

Please proceed with the counter and instruct the customer to sign the security addendum and issue the PO. Loop me if there are any material deviations.

—Aditya Rao
